exposure: Imprinted associated chromosome abnormalities detected by noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT)
outcome: Specific diagnoses of imprinting diseases (e.g., 15q11-q13 duplication syndrome, mosaic trisomy 7, Temple syndrome, absence of heterozygosity)
Pregnancy outcomes (induced labor, spontaneous labor, cesarean section)
Clinical value of NIPT in detecting rare chromosome aneuploidies and microdeletion/microduplication syndromes
cohort: The study included 9 pregnant women whose noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) identified imprinted associated chromosome abnormalities.
finding: Six out of nine fetuses were diagnosed with regional abnormalities of Imprinting Disease, most commonly 15q11-q13 duplication syndrome, demonstrating NIPT's value in detecting rare chromosome aneuploidies and microdeletion/microduplication syndromes in mid-pregnancy.
mod_finding: Among the 9 pregnant women, 4 chose induced labor, 3 chose spontaneous labor, and 2 chose cesarean section.
followup_time: Up to one year after birth or until induction of labor
